questions_and_answers.question: Why couldn't the two teamsters pass each other?

answers.answer: Because the road was narrow and they couldn't easily get out of each other's way.
Because their wagons were broken.
Because one refused to move.
Because they were lost.

questions_and_answers.question: What do the teamsters initially shout at each other?

answers.answer: They greet each other politely.
They ask each other to get out of the way.
They complain about the weather.
They sing a song.

questions_and_answers.question: Why do the teamsters become very angry?

answers.answer: Because both refuse to give in.
Because it starts to rain.
Because one of them is lost.
Because they are late.

questions_and_answers.question: What threat does the first teamster make if the other doesn't move?

answers.answer: He will report him to the authorities.
He will do to him what he did with another person earlier.
He will break his wagon.
He will leave.

questions_and_answers.question: How does the second teamster respond to the threat?

answers.answer: He becomes angry and shouts.
He becomes cautious and asks the first teamster to help push his wagon aside.
He threatens the first teamster.
He leaves immediately.

questions_and_answers.question: What happens after they move the wagon?

answers.answer: They decide to fight.
Everything is in order after a few minutes.
They both leave angrily.
They break the wagon.

questions_and_answers.question: What does the second teamster ask before they drive on?

answers.answer: What his name is.
How the first teamster had dealt with the previous situation he mentioned.
How far the next town is.
If there is a tavern nearby.

questions_and_answers.question: How does the first teamster answer when asked about the earlier situation?

answers.answer: He says he forced the other man off the road.
He says he shouted until the other moved.
He says he got out of the other man's way.
He says he left without doing anything.

questions_and_answers.question: What did the 'Grobian' refuse to do?

answers.answer: He refused to pay a fee.
He refused to get out of the way.
He refused to apologize.
He refused to move his wagon forward.

questions_and_answers.question: What lesson can be inferred from the story?

answers.answer: It is better to remain stubborn.
Being patient and compromising can resolve conflicts.
Always insist on your way.
Avoid narrow roads.

articles.text: Zwei Fuhrleute treffen sich mit ihren Wagen auf einer engen Strasse und können sich nicht gut ausweichen.
"Fahre mir aus dem Wege!" ruft der eine.
"Ei, so fahre du mir aus dem Wege!" ruft der andere.
"Ich brauche es nicht!" sagt der andere.
Keiner gibt nach und sie werden beide sehr ärgerlich.

"Höre", sagt endlich der erste, "jetzt frage ich dich zum letzten Mal: willst du mir aus dem Wege fahren oder nicht? Wenn du es nicht tust, mache ich es mit dir, wie ich es heute schon mit einem anderen gemacht habe."
Der andere Fuhrmann wird vorsichtig und sagt: "Nun, dann hilf mir doch wenigstens deinen Wagen etwas auf die Seite zu schieben, ich habe ja sonst nicht Platz, um mit meinem auszuweichen."
Das ist dem ersten Fuhrmann recht und nach einigen Minuten ist alles in Ordnung.

Bevor sie weiterfahren, fragt der zweite Fuhrmann den ersten: "Hör' mal, vorhin sagtest du doch, du willst es mit mir machen, wie du es heute schon mit einem gemacht hast. Sag' mir doch, wie hast du es mit einem gemacht?"
"Ja, denke dir", sagt der andere, "der Grobian wollte mir nicht aus dem Wege fahren, da fuhr ich ihm aus dem Wege."
(sich) ausweichen — get out of (each other's) way
zum letzten Mal — for the last time
